# Swiss Party for Structural Transformation

> Prosperity, comfort and well-being for all — with a modern social contract that creates security and expands freedom.

Source: https://die-zukunft.ch/en/ · Publisher: The Future (Swiss political party, Basel)

**The Future. We build it.** AI and robotics can create prosperity for everyone. We make sure Switzerland leads this transition: with its own compute, the best talent, production at home and a dividend for everyone.

- Prosperity over scarcity thinking
- Security over fear
- Sovereignty over dependence

## What's changing

Things aren't getting worse – but they are changing. Work, costs, health and security are being redistributed – depending on whether we shape the future or merely react.

- **Work & income**: AI is speeding everything up – and shifting tasks. Administration, logistics, medicine, law: entire professions are transforming. The key question: who gets the productivity gains – and who bears the risk?
- **Housing & everyday life**: Housing remains scarce, commutes get longer, life time is lost. The question isn't city versus countryside, but: how do we get more comfort per square metre – without everything getting more expensive?
- **Health & longevity**: Biotech and prevention are improving – but only with trust. People want innovation without black boxes, with clear consent, auditability and data protection.
- **Digital security**: Payments, identity, communication, public services: our daily life runs on software. When critical systems depend on a few foreign platforms, that's not a tech issue – it's everyday sovereignty.

That's why The Future: we make change plannable – more freedom, less fear, more prosperity.

## What we propose

Thirteen pillars, all at a glance. Each has its own page with concrete measures, goals and indicators.

- [Sovereign AI & Compute](https://die-zukunft.ch/en/sovereign-ai/) (0x2C): Our own compute, open Swiss models and AI that we audit and operate ourselves. The foundation for everything else.
- [Basic Income](https://die-zukunft.ch/en/basic-income/) (0x24): A stable foundation: less bureaucracy, more freedom for retraining, entrepreneurship and care.
- [Work Without Fear](https://die-zukunft.ch/en/transitions/) (0x22): Retraining, mobility and transition support as the norm — not as a last resort.
- [Digital Sovereignty](https://die-zukunft.ch/en/digital-sovereignty/) (0x20): Swiss and European solutions first. Open standards, no vendor lock-in.
- [Re-industrialisation with Robotics](https://die-zukunft.ch/en/robotics/) (0x21): SME-friendly automation: shared labs, incentives, local manufacturing.
- [Life Science & Health](https://die-zukunft.ch/en/life-science/) (0x23): Modern life sciences with consent, auditability and no black-box state medicine.
- [Cities & Housing](https://die-zukunft.ch/en/urban-housing/) (0x25): More affordable housing and quality of life through densification at transit hubs — less sprawl, more comfort.
- [Research, Innovation & Commons](https://die-zukunft.ch/en/research-innovation/) (0x26): Testbeds, open standards and a nationwide innovation network — so innovation has broad impact and doesn't stay in silos.
- [Energy & Infrastructure Resilience](https://die-zukunft.ch/en/energy-resilience/) (0x27): Reliable, affordable, robust supply — resilience through engineering, not ideology.
- [Open Government](https://die-zukunft.ch/en/open-government/) (0x28): API-by-default, radical transparency and open procedures — so citizens can build better tools and effectively scrutinise the state.
- [Neutrality & Peace](https://die-zukunft.ch/en/neutrality-peace/) (0x29): Strictly defensive, credibly neutral — and once again a centre for peace talks and good offices.
- [Talent, Integration & Rule of Law](https://die-zukunft.ch/en/talent-integration/) (0x2A): Open to people who contribute — clear on the rule of law and the rules of coexistence.
- [Language & Understanding](https://die-zukunft.ch/en/language-understanding/) (0x2B): Strengthening national languages, English as a pragmatic bridge — understanding without friction.

## How we start

We start where we live, and we think further ahead than the next election.

- **Phase 1: Basel** (37 km², ≈ 200,000 people): Foundation, first members, local roots in the Basel region.
- **Phase 2: Switzerland** (41,285 km², ≈ 9 million people): Expansion across all language regions, building local chapters and national political work.
- **Phase 3: Europe** (≈ 10 million km², ≈ 745 million people): Partnerships with like-minded movements, shared agenda for a future-ready Europe.
- **Phase 4: Global** (≈ 149 million km² of land, ≈ 8.2 billion people): International network, knowledge transfer and impulses for a new societal policy worldwide.

## Get involved

Join the association, bring your expertise or support us financially. The future is made by people who get to work.

# Manifesto

> Ten theses for the transition into an age of abundance: how Switzerland uses artificial intelligence and robotics so that prosperity reaches everyone.

Source: https://die-zukunft.ch/en/manifesto/ · Publisher: The Future (Swiss political party, Basel)

Version 2.0 · 2026-11-07

## Zero point (0x1001)

For the first time in history, machines can do not only physical work but also cognitive work. Artificial intelligence and robotics will redistribute work, income and power, faster than most institutions can imagine. Switzerland is one of the wealthiest and most capable countries in the world, and yet it talks about this future almost only in the language of fear. This manifesto starts somewhere else: the future is not a fate. It is a construction project. The only open questions are who builds it, by which rules, and for whose benefit.

## 01. Intelligence is becoming infrastructure. (0x1002)

Artificial intelligence makes cognitive work cheap, robotics makes physical work cheap. Whether artificial general intelligence arrives in five years or in twenty: we plan for the case that it comes early. Whoever has compute, models and data shapes the future. Whoever only rents them has to accept it.

→ [Pillar: Sovereign AI & Compute](https://die-zukunft.ch/en/sovereign-ai/)

## 02. Abundance is possible, but not automatic. (0x1003)

For the first time, technology can create enough for everyone: housing, health, time. **Abundance** means prosperity through productivity, not excess through waste. Whether it reaches everyone or only a few is a political decision. Fear is no answer to that. A plan is.

→ [To the vision](https://die-zukunft.ch/en/vision/)

## 03. Compute is sovereignty. (0x1004)

Sovereignty in the 21st century means: our own compute, open Swiss models and enough reliable electricity to run both. Not isolation, but the ability to audit, operate and replace AI ourselves.

→ [Pillar: Digital Sovereignty](https://die-zukunft.ch/en/digital-sovereignty/)

## 04. Production is coming back. (0x1005)

Robots in fields, on building sites and in factories make production in Switzerland competitive again. Local means short distances, know-how in the country and less dependence when the world gets turbulent.

→ [Pillar: Re-industrialisation with Robotics](https://die-zukunft.ch/en/robotics/)

## 05. The state becomes the best service provider in the country. (0x1006)

Open data, open procedures, AI in every public office. Routine cases in minutes, every decision explained and open to appeal. Citizens should be able to read the state, check it and build better tools on top of it.

→ [Pillar: Open Government](https://die-zukunft.ch/en/open-government/)

## 06. No black-box decisions about people. (0x1007)

No automated decision about benefits, treatment or rights without a comprehensible justification, human responsibility and a right of appeal. Fast, but under control: powerful systems are tested before they work in critical areas.

→ [Pillar: Life Science & Health](https://die-zukunft.ch/en/life-science/)

## 07. The dividend belongs to everyone. (0x1008)

When machines do a growing share of the work, part of the gains must flow back to everyone. A basic income as a foundation, retraining as the norm: people without existential fear retrain, start companies and try new things.

→ [Pillar: Basic Income](https://die-zukunft.ch/en/basic-income/)

## 08. Talent is the scarcest resource. (0x1009)

Switzerland has no natural resources, but some of the best universities in the world. We train the people who build AI and robotics, keep them in the country and bring in those who want to build something.

→ [Pillar: Talent, Integration & Rule of Law](https://die-zukunft.ch/en/talent-integration/)

## 09. Engineering instead of ideology. (0x100A)

Not left, not right, but: what works? Hypothesis, pilot, measurement, correction. We disclose what our proposals are based on and change them when the data demands it.

→ [Not left, not right](https://die-zukunft.ch/en/beyond-left-right/)

## 10. Switzerland can be first to make it. (0x100B)

Small enough to learn fast, rich enough to invest, trustworthy enough to be a partner. Strong at home first, then credible abroad: from Basel, we want to show how the transition succeeds, for Switzerland, for Europe and beyond.

→ [Pillar: Neutrality & Peace](https://die-zukunft.ch/en/neutrality-peace/)

## Our commitments (0x100C)

Four promises you can hold us to.

1. **No black-box politics**: No automated decisions about benefits or treatment without a comprehensible justification, human responsibility and a right of appeal.
2. **Sovereign state, open systems**: The state procures critical systems only in ways that keep them auditable, portable and secure. Lock-in is a risk, and it ends.
3. **Change without collapse**: We rebuild the welfare state so that people can switch, learn and start something new without existential fear.
4. **Basic income, pragmatically**: We start with a nationwide pilot and measure the effect: bureaucracy costs, start-ups, well-being.

## What we are not (0x100D)

- **No promises of salvation.** Technology solves nothing by itself. People and institutions do.
- **No enemy images.** We argue about solutions, not about people.
- **No progress without control.** Fast, but comprehensible, verifiable and democratically steerable.
- **No programme of renunciation.** We do not administer scarcity. We end it.

Basel, November 2026. The Future.

### Changelog

- v2.0 (2026-11-07): Ten theses with permanent addresses, focused on AI, robotics and abundance. Commitments carried over unchanged. New: What we are not.
- v1.0 (2026-02-07): First version: summary, convictions, commitments, techno-optimism as a stance.

# Vision

> Artificial intelligence and robotics are changing what work is and where prosperity comes from. The Future is the party that shapes this transition: with compute, sovereign AI, talent and production at home, and with a dividend that reaches everyone.

Source: https://die-zukunft.ch/en/vision/ · Publisher: The Future (Swiss political party, Basel)

**When machines do cognitive and physical work, prosperity for everyone becomes possible. We make sure Switzerland builds it instead of renting it.**

## What is happening right now

Artificial intelligence makes cognitive work cheaper, robotics makes physical work cheaper. It is the biggest economic shift since industrialisation, and Switzerland is less prepared for it than it needs to be.

- **2047 · General AI is getting closer**: In the largest survey of 2,778 AI researchers, the probability that machines will do every task better than humans by 2047 was put at 50 percent. That is 13 years earlier than in the previous survey. Nobody knows when. We plan for the case that it comes early. (Source: [Grace et al., JAIR](https://jair.org/index.php/jair/article/view/19087))
- **294 · Switzerland automates hesitantly**: Robots per 10,000 industrial workers. South Korea has 1,220, Germany 449. Anyone who wants to keep production in the country or bring it back has to automate it. (Source: [IFR World Robotics 2025](https://ifr.org/ifr-press-releases/news/robot-density-surges-in-europe-asia-and-americas))
- **3.6% · Compute needs electricity**: That is the share of Swiss electricity used by data centres in 2024, around 2.1 terawatt hours. By 2030 it could be up to 6 percent. Anyone who wants AI in the country has to plan energy and compute together. (Source: [Swiss Federal Office of Energy, 2026](https://www.admin.ch/de/newnsb/GV-_d7OgIlqjfQDGZqbkN))
- **Rank 26 · The state is falling behind**: In the UN E-Government Index, Switzerland ranked 26th in 2024, down from 16th in 2020. A rich, well-educated country should be among the best here. (Source: [UN E-Government Survey 2024](https://publicadministration.un.org/egovkb/en-us/Data/Country-Information/id/166-Switzerland))

The ingredients are there: with **Apertus**, ETH Zurich, EPFL and CSCS released one of the world's most open large language models in 2025, trained on the **Alps** supercomputer in Lugano with 10,752 GH200 chips. In May 2026 the Swiss Science Council recommended a national AI infrastructure strategy. What is missing is the political will to turn this into a programme.

## Switzerland in 2040

Not science fiction, but what can be achieved with today's technology and political will.

- **Dealing with the authorities in minutes**: Taxes, permits, moving house: the state handles routine cases automatically, with reasons given and a right of appeal. The people in public administration have time for the difficult cases.
- **An AI assistant for everyone**: Everyone in Switzerland has access to a trustworthy AI assistant in their national language, for health, law, education and everyday life. On Swiss infrastructure, with Swiss data protection.
- **The factories come back**: Medicines, precision parts, electronics and food are made in highly automated plants close to us. Shorter supply chains, less dependence, new work in planning, maintenance and development.
- **Building in half the time**: Prefabrication, construction robotics and digital permits bring homes to market faster and more cheaply. More housing is a question of productivity, not of going without.
- **Farms with robots**: Autonomous machines weed, harvest and tend crops with precision. Farms stay productive and independent, even as fewer people work in agriculture.
- **More time, less existential anxiety**: The gains from automation flow back to everyone as a dividend: a foundation that makes retraining, starting a business and care work possible.

## The abundance stack

Prosperity from AI does not come from an app. It comes from layers that build on each other. If one is missing, the whole thing does not hold. That is why we think them through together, from energy to the dividend.

01. **Energy**: No electricity, no compute and no robots. We secure affordable, reliable electricity, including in winter, and plan for the additional demand from data centres and automation from the start. → https://die-zukunft.ch/en/energy-resilience/
02. **Compute**: Data centres and AI capacity in the country, accessible to universities, SMEs and public administration. If you only rent compute, you rent your future. → https://die-zukunft.ch/en/sovereign-ai/
03. **Sovereign AI**: Develop open Swiss models like Apertus further, in all national languages and with transparent data. For critical applications the rule is: models we can audit, operate and replace. → https://die-zukunft.ch/en/sovereign-ai/
04. **Talent**: Train, retain and attract the best people: strengthen ETH, EPFL and the universities of applied sciences, more permits for skilled workers from third countries, retraining as the norm. → https://die-zukunft.ch/en/talent-integration/
05. **Application in every sector**: Robots in fields, on building sites and in factories. AI in every service and in public administration. Wherever it takes load off people and brings value creation into the country. → https://die-zukunft.ch/en/robotics/
06. **Dividend**: The productivity gains reach everyone: through a basic income as a foundation, safe transitions between occupations and lower everyday costs. → https://die-zukunft.ch/en/basic-income/

## Three sectors, one goal

Machines should work where they take load off people and bring value creation into the country. In every sector of the economy.

### Primary sector · Agriculture & raw materials: Precision instead of drudgery

Agriculture is losing workers: almost 30 percent fewer people have worked in it since 2000. Robotics keeps farms productive and food supply in the country.

- Autonomous weeding, tending and harvesting robots
- Shared machinery pools for small and medium-sized farms
- Sensors for precise use of water and fertiliser
- Automated processing close to the farm

### Secondary sector · Industry & construction: Production comes back

Highly automated manufacturing makes production in Switzerland competitive again, despite high wages. Local means: short distances, less dependence, know-how in the country.

- Fully automated plants for medtech, pharma, precision and electronics
- Shared robotics centres for SMEs
- Construction robotics and industrial prefabrication
- Being able to make critical goods in the country

### Tertiary sector · Services & the state: Every service gets better

AI makes services faster, cheaper and more accessible. The state leads the way and becomes the best service provider in the country.

- Administration: routine cases automated, every decision explained
- AI assistance in health, law and education
- Lower costs in banking, insurance and retail
- More time for the personal, the complex and the caring

## Fast, but under control

People adopt new technology when they can trust it. That is why clear rules apply for us.

- **Human responsibility.** Every decision about people has a responsible person, a stated reason and a right of appeal.
- **Auditability.** AI in public use is documented, tested and independently auditable.
- **Privacy by design.** Health and personal data only with consent. Critical processing in the country.
- **Safety before scale.** Powerful systems are tested for risks before they are deployed in critical areas.
- **Freedom of choice.** Personal access to public services remains guaranteed for everyone who needs it.

## Why Switzerland can be first to make it

- **World-class research**: ETH Zurich is one of the ten best universities in the world. With EPFL, CSCS and Apertus, Switzerland has what other countries still have to build.
- **Small and decentralised**: 26 cantons are 26 real-world laboratories. What works in one, the others can adopt. That way a country learns faster than one big centre.
- **Trust and democracy**: Direct democracy gives change legitimacy. What the population helps decide, it also carries.
- **Industry with precision**: Medtech, pharma, mechanical engineering: Switzerland can build complex things. Automation makes this strength bigger, not smaller.
- **Reliable energy**: More than half of Swiss electricity comes from dispatchable hydropower. That is a good basis for data centres, if we plan the expansion wisely.
- **Neutrality**: A neutral country under the rule of law is a trustworthy place for compute, data and international AI diplomacy.

## The party for this transition.

The established parties argue about how today's pie is divided. AI appears for them as a risk, as a regulatory question, or not at all. Yet the next ten years will decide who owns tomorrow's value creation.

**The Future** puts this question at the centre. We understand the technology, we take its risks seriously, and we have a plan for how Switzerland uses it: with its own compute, its own models, the best talent, production in the country and a dividend for everyone.

Not left, not right. Forward.

## What you can measure us by

Goals with a year attached. We report publicly on how far Switzerland has come.

- **2027**: National AI infrastructure strategy with secured funding. As recommended by the Science Council in 2026: compute as permanent infrastructure, not as time-limited project money.
- **2027**: Twice as many permits for skilled workers from third countries. From 8,500 to 17,000 per year, targeted at research, AI, robotics and health.
- **2028**: An open Swiss AI model in use in the federal administration. Based on Apertus, operated on Swiss infrastructure, in all national languages.
- **2028**: Nationwide basic income pilot under way. With independent evaluation of bureaucracy costs, business start-ups and well-being.
- **2030**: Ten times more publicly accessible AI computing capacity. For universities, SMEs and public administration, with the electricity demand planned in from the start.
- **2030**: Among the top ten countries in the UN E-Government Index. Rank 26 today. Routine cases digital and automated, with reasons given and a right of appeal.
- **2035**: Robot density in industry doubled. From 294 to around 600 robots per 10,000 workers, ahead of Germany at 449 today.

# Program

> Our political program for structural transformation.

Source: https://die-zukunft.ch/en/program/ · Publisher: The Future (Swiss political party, Basel)

### [Sovereign AI & Compute](https://die-zukunft.ch/en/sovereign-ai/)

Compute is the infrastructure of the 21st century. Our own AI capacity, open Swiss models like Apertus and the ability to audit and operate AI ourselves. Accessible to universities, SMEs and public administration.

### [Digital Sovereignty](https://die-zukunft.ch/en/digital-sovereignty/)

Critical digital systems must remain under democratic control. Swiss/EU-first for critical infrastructure and sensitive data. Anti-lock-in, open source, supply-chain security.

### [Re-industrialisation with Robotics](https://die-zukunft.ch/en/robotics/)

More production and value creation in Switzerland — robust, modern, automated. SME-friendly with financing, shared labs and faster procedures.

### [Work Without Fear](https://die-zukunft.ch/en/transitions/)

Retraining, professional mobility and transition support as the norm — not only in crisis. Fewer hurdles, better recognition, modular education.

### [Life Science & Health](https://die-zukunft.ch/en/life-science/)

Enabling progress — without losing control. Health data opt-in, evidence-based regulation, no black-box state medicine.

### [Basic Income](https://die-zukunft.ch/en/basic-income/)

Reducing existential fear, lowering bureaucracy, enabling entrepreneurship. A federal pilot with independent evaluation.

### [Cities & Housing](https://die-zukunft.ch/en/urban-housing/)

Affordable housing and high quality of life — through densification where infrastructure exists, and less sprawl in the periphery. More building rights at transit hubs, fast-track permits, minimum densities.

### [Research, Innovation & Commons](https://die-zukunft.ch/en/research-innovation/)

Switzerland should be the place where serious innovation can be built, tested and responsibly scaled fastest — with clear public benefit and European compatibility.

### [Energy & Infrastructure Resilience](https://die-zukunft.ch/en/energy-resilience/)

Reliable supply, robust infrastructure and predictable costs — as the foundation for prosperity, comfort and sovereignty. Resilience is engineering: clear standards, clear responsibilities, clear redundancies.

### [Open Government](https://die-zukunft.ch/en/open-government/)

A state that enables rather than blocks: API-by-default, radical transparency and open procedures — so citizens can build better tools and effectively scrutinise the state.

### [Neutrality & Peace](https://die-zukunft.ch/en/neutrality-peace/)

Switzerland remains neutral, sovereign and credible — and once again becomes a place where peace is negotiated. Strictly defensive, good offices, diplomacy and humanitarian strength.

### [Talent, Integration & Rule of Law](https://die-zukunft.ch/en/talent-integration/)

Switzerland should be a magnet for people who want to build something — and at the same time remain a country where security, order and trust are self-evident.

### [Language & Understanding](https://die-zukunft.ch/en/language-understanding/)

Switzerland should become the European model for understanding: more shared communication in everyday life and business — without displacing national languages.

## Our program for transformation

Our program addresses the central challenges of structural change — pragmatic, measurable and tailored to Swiss conditions.

---

# Sovereign AI & Compute

> Compute is the infrastructure of the 21st century. Switzerland needs its own capacity, open models and the ability to audit and operate AI itself.

Source: https://die-zukunft.ch/en/sovereign-ai/ · Publisher: The Future (Swiss political party, Basel)

## Why this matters now

AI is becoming the foundation of public administration, health, industry and research. Without its own computing capacity and its own models, a country depends on a few foreign providers: on their prices, their rules and their off switches. With the Alps supercomputer and the open language model Apertus, Switzerland has an excellent starting position. What is missing is a strategy that turns this into national infrastructure.

## Our principles

- **Compute is infrastructure**, like roads and electricity, not time-limited project money.
- **Open where possible:** open weights, open training data, open code.
- **Sovereign where necessary:** critical applications run on systems we can audit, operate and replace.
- **Accessible to all:** universities, SMEs, municipalities and schools, not just corporations.

## The AI infrastructure package

### 1. National computing capacity

- Increase publicly accessible AI computing capacity tenfold by 2030
- Long-term funding instead of time-limited project money, as recommended by the Science Council in 2026
- Fast permits for data centres with waste-heat recovery and a secure electricity supply

### 2. Sovereign models

- Develop Apertus and its successors further as open Swiss foundation models
- All national languages, including Romansh and Swiss German
- Public access for the population, schools and SMEs, not just for research

### 3. AI in the state

- Secure AI tools on Swiss infrastructure for every administrative unit
- Routine cases automated, every decision explained and open to appeal
- Open tenders instead of lock-in to individual AI providers

### 4. Audit and safeguard

- A national AI testing lab for safety, robustness and fairness
- Clear liability and human responsibility for decisions about people
- Sector-specific rules instead of blanket bans, in line with the Council of Europe's AI Convention

## What this means in everyday life

- An AI assistant in your language, whose data stays in Switzerland
- Faster, clearer answers from the authorities
- SMEs that can use AI without tying themselves to one corporation
- Research that creates companies and jobs in Switzerland

## Indicators

- **2027**: National AI infrastructure strategy with secured funding
- **2028**: An open Swiss model in use in the federal administration
- **2030**: Ten times more publicly accessible AI computing capacity than today

## Frequently asked questions

**Can Switzerland keep up with the US and China?**  
Not across the board, and it doesn't need to. It needs to be able to audit and adapt models itself and to operate them for critical tasks. With Alps, ETH, EPFL and open models like Apertus, that is realistic.

**Why not simply use the best models from the big providers?**  
For many applications, that is exactly what we do. But for critical areas such as public administration, health and justice, we need systems we can audit and keep running, even if prices, laws or political relations abroad change.

**Don't data centres use too much electricity?**  
In 2024, data centres used around 3.6 percent of Swiss electricity, and the trend is rising. That is why we plan for the demand: efficiency standards, use of waste heat and additional, reliable generation, especially in winter.

**What about artificial general intelligence (AGI)?**  
Nobody knows when systems will arrive that can handle almost any cognitive task at human level. Many researchers consider it likely within the next few decades, some much sooner. We are aligning policy so that Switzerland is prepared in either case: with its own capacity, the ability to audit, and a dividend that shares the gains.

**Does sovereign mean shutting ourselves off?**  
No. Sovereign means having alternatives. We work with Europe and the world, and open models are ideal for that. But critical systems must not depend on a single provider or state.

---

# Digital Sovereignty

> Sovereignty starts with infrastructure: open, auditable, portable — and secure.

Source: https://die-zukunft.ch/en/digital-sovereignty/ · Publisher: The Future (Swiss political party, Basel)

## Digital Infrastructure

Digital systems are infrastructure today, like roads and electricity: when they are opaque, insecure or non-cancellable, democracy loses control.

## Our Principle

Swiss/EU-first only for critical infrastructure and sensitive data. Otherwise: open competition — but always with auditability, portability and security as requirements.

## The Sovereignty Package

### 1. Anti-Lock-in Law

- Exit plans as a contractual requirement
- Open standards and format interfaces
- Data portability and interoperability

### 2. Open-by-default in Government

- Open source where sensible (and maintainable)
- Funding for maintenance (not just "build and forget")
- Transparency reports on large government IT systems (risks, dependencies, exit status)

### 3. Security of Critical Systems

- Minimum standard: controls, audits, incident processes
- Supply-chain security: SBOM, signed builds, traceable provenance
- Clear responsibilities instead of jurisdictional fog

## Why This Improves Everyday Life

- Fewer IT investment failures
- Less dependency on individual vendors
- Lower risk in critical services
- More trust through transparency

## Frequently asked questions

**What does digital sovereignty mean in practice?**  
Digital sovereignty means that the state and its citizens retain control over their data, systems and digital infrastructure — independent of individual vendors or countries.

**Does that mean we can no longer use foreign software?**  
No. Swiss/EU-first applies only to critical infrastructure and sensitive data. For everything else: open competition — but always with mandatory auditability, portability and open standards.

**What is an anti-lock-in law?**  
A law that prevents the state from permanently tying itself to a single IT vendor. It requires exit plans, open formats and data portability as contractual obligations.

**Isn't open source more expensive than commercial solutions?**  
Not necessarily. Open source reduces long-term costs through less licence dependency. What matters is that maintenance is also funded — not just the initial deployment.

**How does this affect everyday life?**  
Fewer IT failures in public services, fewer data breaches, more transparency. And no surprises when a vendor suddenly doubles prices or discontinues their service.

---

# Re-industrialisation with Robotics

> More production and value creation in Switzerland: automated, local, SME-friendly. In the field, on the building site and in the factory.

Source: https://die-zukunft.ch/en/robotics/ · Publisher: The Future (Swiss political party, Basel)

## Why Re-industrialisation?

If we want to bring production back, it must be modern: automated, efficient, resilient. With 294 robots per 10,000 industrial workers, Switzerland lags far behind South Korea (1,220) and also behind Germany (449). Highly automated manufacturing makes production competitive again despite high wages. This is an opportunity, especially for SMEs.

## Robots in Every Sector

Robotics is not just a topic for the factory floor. It takes load off people wherever work is physically hard, dangerous or short of hands.

### Agriculture

Almost 30 percent fewer people have worked in agriculture since 2000. Robotics keeps farms productive.

- Autonomous weeding, tending and harvesting robots
- Shared machinery pools so that small farms can afford robotics too
- Automated processing close to the farm

### Construction

Building faster means more housing at lower cost.

- Industrial prefabrication of components and modules
- Construction robotics for heavy, repetitive and dangerous work
- Digital building permits based on building information models

### Industry

Switzerland can build complex things. Automation makes this strength bigger.

- Fully automated plants for medtech, pharma, precision and electronics
- Being able to make critical goods in the country: medicines, components, food
- Maintenance, planning and development as new, well-paid industrial occupations

## Producing Locally

Production belongs close to the people who need it. Regional, automated plants shorten supply chains, keep know-how in the country and make Switzerland less dependent on global disruptions. Local does not mean isolated: we keep exporting what we do best.

## Our Priorities

- **Health & Life-Science Supply**: Medtech, pharma-adjacent production
- **Industrial Core**: Precision engineering, toolmaking, electronics/packaging
- **Resilience Basics**: Food/agri-tech, grid and supply security

## The SME Package

Financing first: affordable loans, guarantees, co-investments for modernisation and (re-)shoring.

- Tax incentives for automation investments
- Shared robotics labs / automation centres
- Training and upskilling vouchers
- Faster permits for modern production facilities
- Procurement advantages for critical goods (where appropriate)
- Regulatory sandboxes for automation

## Our Goal

Double robot density in Swiss industry by 2035, from 294 to around 600 robots per 10,000 workers. And grow industrial value creation in the country again, measured publicly every year.

## Automation in the Services Sector

We are pro-automation when it relieves people and increases productivity — with the clear goal: more time, more freedom, more prosperity.

## Frequently asked questions

**Will robots take people's jobs?**  
Not if we do it right. Automation frees people from monotonous and dangerous work. The key lies in retraining, basic income and new job profiles.

**Do only large corporations benefit from robotics?**  
No — that's exactly what we want to prevent. Our SME package includes shared robotics labs, affordable loans and training vouchers so small businesses can automate too.

**What does re-industrialisation mean for Switzerland?**  
More local value creation, shorter supply chains and less dependence on global disruptions. Production in Switzerland — modern, automated and competitive.

**Which sectors should be automated?**  
Wherever it makes sense: medtech, precision manufacturing, food tech, logistics. Not as an end in itself, but where automation improves quality, efficiency and resilience.

**Doesn't this require highly qualified specialists?**  
Yes — which is why training programmes are part of the package. Robotics expertise must not be elite knowledge. Shared labs and modular courses make entry accessible.

---

# Work Without Fear

> Career changes, learning, fresh starts as the norm — not the exception.

Source: https://die-zukunft.ch/en/transitions/ · Publisher: The Future (Swiss political party, Basel)

## Work Without Fear

Upskilling and career changes must become normal: fewer hurdles, more support, clear prospects. Those who adapt deserve a safety net — not a bureaucratic maze.

## What Must Change

### Fewer Bureaucratic Hurdles

Retraining shouldn't be an obstacle course. Applications must be simpler, approvals faster and funding more accessible.

### Better Recognition of Skills and Certificates

Work experience and further training count — even when they don't come from the traditional education system. Competence over diplomas.

### Combining Learning and Work

Part-time models, work-integrated education and modular training must be promoted — for all life stages, not just career starters.

### Focus: Results, Not Forms

Less administration, more impact. Support programmes should be measured by outcomes, not by the number of forms filled in.

## Why This Is Urgent

- Technology is changing job profiles faster than education systems can respond
- People need security to embrace the new
- Transitions are becoming the norm — the system must keep up

## Frequently asked questions

**What are 'transitions'?**  
Career changes, retraining, fresh starts — everything that happens when job profiles evolve. We want this to be normal and supported, not anxiety-inducing and bureaucratic.

**Who pays for retraining?**  
A combination of employer contributions, public funds and new financing models. The goal: nobody should have to forgo training for financial reasons.

**Why aren't current systems sufficient?**  
Because they're too slow, too bureaucratic and designed for exceptions. In a world where job profiles change every few years, transitions must be the norm — not the exception.

**What does 'competence before credentials' mean?**  
That practical skills and work experience are recognised equally — not just formal qualifications. If you can do something, you should be able to prove it, regardless of your educational path.

**Does this only apply to technical professions?**  
No. Transitions affect all sectors: healthcare, trades, administration, services. Everywhere that automation and digitalisation are transforming job profiles.

---

# Life Science & Health

> Enabling progress — with transparency, consent and control.

Source: https://die-zukunft.ch/en/life-science/ · Publisher: The Future (Swiss political party, Basel)

## Progress with Trust

Life sciences are opening new possibilities — from personalised therapies to prevention, from new diagnostics to industrial biotechnology. Switzerland is a world leader in this field. For this to continue, clear rules that build trust are needed.

## Our Principles

### Health Data: Opt-in as Standard

Health data belongs to people, not to the state and not to industry. The standard is opt-in, with narrow exceptions only for public health.

### Regulation: Evidence-based and Traceable

New therapies and technologies are assessed case-by-case — based on evidence, not ideology. Regulatory decisions must be traceable and justified.

### Partnerships: Yes — but with Transparency Rules

Collaboration between government, research and industry is important. But every partnership needs clear transparency rules: who finances? Who decides? Who benefits?

## Red Lines

**No black-box state**: No automated decisions about medical services or treatments without traceable reasoning, human responsibility and the right to appeal.

## Why This Matters

- Switzerland as a pharma and biotech hub needs a clear framework
- Citizens deserve control over their health data
- Innovation and trust are not contradictory — they are prerequisites for each other

## Frequently asked questions

**Who owns health data?**  
The people themselves — not the state and not industry. The standard is opt-in: data is used only with explicit consent, with narrow exceptions for public health.

**Don't clear rules slow down research?**  
No — trust is the precondition for people sharing their data at all. Switzerland stays a leader only if innovation and trust go together: each is the condition for the other.

**What does 'no black-box state medicine' mean?**  
No automated decisions about medical services or treatments without traceable reasoning, human responsibility and the right to appeal. That is a red line.

**Where do we stand on partnerships with industry?**  
Collaboration between government, research and industry is important — but every partnership needs clear transparency rules: who finances? Who decides? Who benefits?

**How are new therapies regulated?**  
Evidence-based and case-by-case: data instead of ideology. Regulatory decisions must be traceable and justified.

---

# Basic Income

> Basic income as the automation dividend: stability, freedom, simplification.

Source: https://die-zukunft.ch/en/basic-income/ · Publisher: The Future (Swiss political party, Basel)

## The Automation Dividend

When machines produce a growing share of value, part of this dividend must flow back to society. Basic income is not charity — it is a structural answer to a structural change.

## What It Enables

- **Freedom to Retrain**: Those who lose their job need a bridge, not fear.
- **Entrepreneurship-friendly**: A stable foundation enables risk-taking for new ideas.
- **Recognising Care Work**: Unpaid care work is made visible through financial security.
- **Cutting Bureaucracy**: Dozens of individual benefits are replaced by a transparent system.
- **Flexible Work**: Part-time, project work or further education become possible without existential fear.

## Not an Experiment — an Evolution

Switzerland has one of the best social systems in the world. Basic income builds on it: simpler, more direct, more contemporary. It is the logical evolution for a society in transition.

## Frequently asked questions

**Isn't this just 'money for everyone'?**  
No. Basic income replaces a large part of today's social insurance bureaucracy with a simple, universal basic security. It is a simplification of the system — not a handout.

**How is it financed?**  
Not through a special robot tax — automation is not punished. It is financed through the normal taxation of growing value creation (income, consumption, wealth), through simplification gains in the social system, and by reallocating existing transfers — exactly the levers our UBI Calculator models. Concrete models are developed with economists and social scientists.

**Will people stop working?**  
Research shows: no. Pilot projects worldwide demonstrate that people with basic security start businesses more often, pursue further education and work more productively — not less.

**Why now?**  
Automation is accelerating. Without a stabilising foundation, social disruption threatens. Basic income is a preventive measure, not a reactive one.

**Does it apply to non-Swiss residents?**  
The exact design — such as residency requirements and contribution periods — will be determined through democratic process. The key is the principle of universal basic security.

**What happens to existing social benefits?**  
Basic income replaces and simplifies existing transfer payments. The goal is not to add more on top, but to make the system simpler, more transparent and fairer.

**Why a pilot and not immediate implementation?**  
Because we are pragmatic. A federal pilot compares models (UBI, negative income tax, hybrid), measures impact and creates a solid basis for decision-making — instead of ideology.

**What is measured?**  
Three core areas: well-being and security (existential stress, stability), entrepreneurship and startups, and bureaucracy costs and administrative burden.

---

# Cities & Housing

> Affordable housing and quality of life through densification at transit hubs — less sprawl, more comfort.

Source: https://die-zukunft.ch/en/urban-housing/ · Publisher: The Future (Swiss political party, Basel)

## Cities & Housing

Prosperity and comfort are felt in everyday life: short commutes, affordable housing, less stress, more quality of life. For this, cities must be able to grow — **upward and inward**, not endlessly outward.

## Our Principle

**Densify where infrastructure exists.** This preserves landscape and village character — and curbs sprawl.

## Three Immediate Measures

### 1) More Building Rights at Transit Hubs

Around stations and strong tram and bus corridors, more storeys and higher utilisation should be possible. Those who want city life must be allowed to build it — where it works.

### 2) Fast-track Permits for Dense Housing Projects

Good projects often fail not due to engineering, but due to time and process. We want clear deadlines, unified responsibilities and a one-stop process.

### 3) Minimum Densities in Defined Zones

Near stations and along central corridors, densification should be the norm. This creates supply — and eases pressure on peripheral areas.

## Height: Yes, but with Rules

The goal is not a skyline — but **housing, comfort and proximity**.

- **High-rises** in clearly defined zones (centres/stations) — with strong quality and design requirements.
- **Mid-rise** (e.g. 6–10 storeys) as the standard where it makes urban sense.

## Affordability Without Ideology

Affordability comes from a mix:

- More supply through targeted densification
- Complement through cooperatives and non-profit providers
- Stable rental models and planning certainty

## Why This Is Future Policy

- Less commuting stress, less time lost
- More integration: the city as a place of encounter and opportunity
- More nature stays nature — because we don't need to sprawl

## Frequently asked questions

**Why densification instead of building on greenfields?**  
Densify where infrastructure exists: that creates housing with short commutes while preserving landscape and village character. Sprawl makes commutes longer and infrastructure more expensive.

**Does that mean high-rises everywhere?**  
No. High-rises only in clearly defined zones (centres, stations) with strong quality requirements; the standard is mid-rise (6–10 storeys) where it makes urban sense. The goal is not a skyline, but housing, comfort and proximity.

**How does this make housing more affordable?**  
Through more supply in the right places — complemented by cooperatives, non-profit providers and stable rental models. Scarcity is the biggest price driver.

**What are fast-track permits?**  
Clear deadlines, unified responsibilities and a one-stop process for dense housing projects. Today, good projects often fail not due to engineering, but due to time and process.

**What do people outside the cities gain?**  
Less pressure on peripheral areas and surrounding rents, less sprawl — and more nature that stays nature.

---

# Research, Innovation & Commons

> Switzerland as the best place for responsible innovation — transparent, interoperable, European-compatible.

Source: https://die-zukunft.ch/en/research-innovation/ · Publisher: The Future (Swiss political party, Basel)

## Research, Innovation & Commons

Prosperity emerges where new things can be built — quickly, responsibly and with real benefit. Switzerland can do this better than almost any country, if politics modernises the framework.

## Our Goal

Switzerland should be the **best place** to develop and scale innovation — transparently, auditably, interoperably — and at the same time **European-compatible**.

## Three Levers

### 1) Testbeds & Sandboxes

New solutions should be trialled in clearly bounded test environments — with measurable goals, transparent evaluation and real learning loops.

### 2) Public Return from Public Funding

When tax money supports innovation, the benefit must be broadly shared:

- Open standards and interoperability as the default
- Knowledge transfer instead of silos
- Responsible IP models (where sensible)
- "Maintenance" built in: not just build, but operate

### 3) Nationwide Innovation Network

We connect universities, polytechnics, startups, SMEs and industry across cantons — with clear rules, transparent governance and fast implementation pathways. Where European cooperation is beneficial, we use it.

## Why This Fits Us

Innovation is not an end in itself. It is a means for:

- Better public services
- A more productive economy
- More prosperity and comfort for all

## Frequently asked questions

**What is a testbed?**  
A clearly bounded test environment where new solutions are trialled under real conditions — with measurable goals, transparent evaluation and real learning loops.

**Why 'commons'?**  
When tax money supports innovation, the benefit must be broadly shared: open standards and interoperability as the default, knowledge transfer instead of silos, and responsible IP models where sensible.

**How does this differ from today's innovation funding?**  
We build in operations: maintenance is funded, not just construction; results are evaluated transparently; and a nationwide innovation network connects universities, startups, SMEs and industry across cantons.

**Why does European compatibility matter?**  
Innovation scales across markets and standards. Where European cooperation increases impact, we use it — without giving up Swiss autonomy.

# Energy & Infrastructure Resilience

> Reliable, affordable and independent infrastructure as the foundation for prosperity and sovereignty.

Source: https://die-zukunft.ch/en/energy-resilience/ · Publisher: The Future (Swiss political party, Basel)

## Energy & Infrastructure Resilience

Comfort means: things work. Electricity, networks, mobility, critical supply — reliably, affordably, robustly. This is the foundation for prosperity.

## Our Goal

Resilient infrastructure in Switzerland that better absorbs outages and crises and makes costs more predictable — without ideology, without alarmism.

## Our Priorities

### 1) Reliability as the Key Metric

Infrastructure planning should focus more on uptime, peak-load capability and recoverability.

### 2) Faster Procedures for Critical Projects

When a project improves supply security, it must not get stuck in endless loops: clear responsibilities, clear deadlines, clear decisions.

### 3) Reduce Critical Dependencies

Where disruptions are costly, we secure components, spare parts and know-how — pragmatically and risk-based. Where cooperation with European partners increases resilience, we pursue it.

## Principle

Resilience is **engineering**: standards, redundancy, testing, accountability.

## Frequently asked questions

**What does 'resilience is engineering' mean?**  
Reliability is not a creed, it's a craft: clear standards, redundancy, testing and accountability. We measure infrastructure by uptime, peak-load capability and recoverability.

**Why faster procedures?**  
Projects that improve supply security must not get stuck in endless loops: clear responsibilities, clear deadlines, clear decisions.

**What are critical dependencies?**  
Components, spare parts and know-how whose failure is costly. We secure them pragmatically and risk-based — and pursue cooperation with European partners where it increases resilience.

**Does this make energy more expensive?**  
The goal is the opposite: predictable costs. Outages and crises end up costing more than redundancy — resilience is an investment in stable prices and reliable supply.

---

# Open Government

> A state that enables rather than blocks: data and procedures open, machine-readable and available via APIs.

Source: https://die-zukunft.ch/en/open-government/ · Publisher: The Future (Swiss political party, Basel)

## Open Government: API-by-default

The state is a service provider for democracy. When data and processes are stuck in silos, gatekeeping emerges: slow, expensive, opaque. That doesn't fit the future. The state makes everything that doesn't concern national security **openly, machine-readably and via APIs** available — so citizens, media and businesses can build solutions that simplify processes and strengthen oversight.

## API-by-default

Agencies publish data not just as PDFs, but as reliable interfaces:

- Unified standards (formats, identifiers)
- Clear versioning and change logs
- Stable availability (service level)
- Documentation, examples, open-source reference clients

## "Open Procedures" Instead of Bureaucratic Jungle

Every process is described digitally as a workflow:

- Requirements and documents
- Deadlines and status
- Fees
- Clear responsibilities

## Transparency as Standard

Transparency should not depend on goodwill, but be standard:

- Budgets and expenditure
- Procurement and contracts (where possible)
- Government KPIs (processing times etc.)
- Job profiles and salary bands (where sensible)

## Transparency in Politics

For democracy to stay clean, clarity is needed:

- Party financing and donation flows
- Campaign budgets and major funders
- Timely and public

## Citizen Oversight in the 21st Century

Citizen journalists, NGOs, researchers and interested citizens should be able to effectively scrutinise the state. A modern state is not afraid of oversight — it gets better because of it.

- Open data
- Dashboards
- Audit logs and traceable decisions

## Our Guardrails

So this doesn't become dangerous:

- **National Security**: remains protected.
- **Privacy-by-design**: minimise personal data, anonymise/aggregate.
- **Security-by-design**: strong standards, audits, clear accountability.
- **No Black-box State**: Decisions must be traceable, contestable and accountable.

## Why This Increases Prosperity and Comfort

- Less paper and waiting time
- Lower administrative costs
- Better services through competition and innovation
- More trust through transparency

## Frequently asked questions

**What does API-by-default mean?**  
Authorities publish data and procedures not just as PDFs, but as reliable, documented interfaces — with unified standards, versioning and stable availability. Everything that doesn't concern national security is open and machine-readable.

**Isn't this a privacy risk?**  
No — openness applies to the state's data and processes, not to personal data. Privacy-by-design applies (minimise, anonymise, aggregate), as does security-by-design (strong standards, audits, clear responsibilities).

**What does this deliver in everyday life?**  
Less paperwork and waiting, lower administrative costs and better services — because citizens, media and companies can build better tools on open data.

**Does transparency also apply to politics itself?**  
Yes: party financing, donation flows and campaign budgets should be publicly viewable, promptly. That applies to us too.

---

# Neutrality & Peace

> Switzerland remains neutral, sovereign and credible — and once again becomes a place where peace is negotiated.

Source: https://die-zukunft.ch/en/neutrality-peace/ · Publisher: The Future (Swiss political party, Basel)

## Neutrality & Peace

Switzerland has a unique strategic advantage: credibility through neutrality and a tradition of good offices and international mediation. This is not a myth — it is a strategic asset.

## Strong at Home First, Then Credible Abroad

We want Switzerland to work internally: secure, resilient, sovereign. Only then can it credibly help externally. Our ambition is to lead by example — not to lecture.

## What Neutrality Means to Us

- No participation in wars between states
- No offensive military adventures
- Active peace work: mediate, host, support humanitarian efforts

## Why a Protection and Resilience Focus Makes Sense

Threats have changed: hybrid risks, sabotage, cyber attacks, system failures. Critical infrastructure is the nervous system of modern Switzerland. Therefore: expand protection capability without becoming aggressive:

- Protect critical infrastructure (IT/OT, energy, communication, supply)
- Support civilian authorities in crises
- Clear, defensive doctrine
- High professionalism and democratic control

## Switzerland as Host and Facilitator for Peace

We want to strengthen Switzerland's role as host for talks, negotiations and agreements — with International Geneva as a platform, and with a consistent policy of good offices.

## Guardrails

- Strictly defensive: protection, not projection
- Neutral and credible: no tribal politics
- Transparent and rule-of-law: clear mandates, clear responsibilities

## Frequently asked questions

**Isn't neutrality outdated?**  
On the contrary: credible neutrality is a strategic asset. It makes Switzerland the place where conflict parties can still talk to each other — a role we want to strengthen, with International Geneva as the platform.

**Does neutral mean defenceless?**  
No. Strictly defensive means: building protective capability without becoming aggressive — protecting critical infrastructure, supporting civilian authorities in crises, with a clear doctrine and democratic control.

**What are good offices?**  
The Swiss tradition of making peace possible: hosting talks and negotiations, mediating and providing humanitarian support.

**What does 'strong at home first, then credible abroad' mean?**  
Switzerland must first work domestically: secure, resilient, sovereign. Only then can it help credibly abroad. Our ambition is to lead by example — not to lecture.

**How does this fit the new threats?**  
Hybrid risks, sabotage and cyberattacks target the nervous system of modern Switzerland: its critical infrastructure. That's why neutrality and resilience belong together — protection instead of projection.

# Talent, Integration & Rule of Law

> Openness for talent and clear rules — Switzerland as a hub for people who want to contribute.

Source: https://die-zukunft.ch/en/talent-integration/ · Publisher: The Future (Swiss political party, Basel)

## Talent, Integration & Rule of Law

Switzerland thrives on stability, quality and trust — and on people who contribute. We want to strengthen both: **openness for talent** and **clear rules** that apply to everyone.

## Switzerland as a Hub for International Talent

We want people from around the world to be able to research, found companies, work and invest in Switzerland — and for our location to become stronger as a result. This is part of our prosperity model.

## Integration Means Commitment

Those who move to Switzerland should not just "be here", but **arrive here**:

- Learn the language and orient themselves
- Access to work and education
- Participation in social life

## Rule of Law and Security

Rules are the foundation of our trust. Clear, fair, without hysteria:

- Expectations are clear and apply to everyone
- Violations are consistently enforced under the rule of law
- No generalisations based on origin — responsibility is individual

## Why This Fits The Future

Abundance and comfort emerge in a society that is **open** to capability and commitment — and **reliable** in its rules. Exactly this combination makes Switzerland strong.

## Frequently asked questions

**Do you want more or less migration?**  
That's the wrong question. We want Switzerland to be open to people who contribute — researchers, founders, skilled professionals — while staying reliable in its rules. The quality of integration is what counts, not symbolic debates.

**What does 'integration means commitment' mean?**  
Those who move to Switzerland should truly arrive: learn the language, have access to work and training, take part in social life. It is both an expectation and an offer.

**And those who don't follow the rules?**  
Rules apply to everyone, and violations are consistently prosecuted under the rule of law. But responsibility is individual — no generalisations by origin.

**Why is talent inflow part of the prosperity model?**  
Because prosperity emerges where skill and effort are welcome. People who research, found and invest here make the country stronger — and everyone benefits.

# Language & Understanding

> Switzerland as a model for clear communication, strong diversity and integration without friction.

Source: https://die-zukunft.ch/en/language-understanding/ · Publisher: The Future (Swiss political party, Basel)

## Language & Understanding

Switzerland is multilingual — and precisely because of this, we know: language is infrastructure. It determines whether people feel welcome, whether work succeeds, whether institutions are comprehensible.

## Our Goal

Switzerland should become the model in Europe for:

- Clear, simple communication
- Strong cultural diversity
- Integration without friction

## National Languages Stay

We don't want to displace any national language. German, French, Italian (and Romansh) are part of Switzerland. At the same time, we need an **additional shared lingua franca** to facilitate cooperation nationwide and internationally.

## Why English Is the Pragmatic Choice

English is today's most practical bridge language:

- Science and innovation
- International business
- Mobility and exchange in Europe and globally

## Implementation: Step by Step and Measurable

- Multilingual government information (incl. English) where it has impact
- Voluntary learning pathways and recognition of language competences
- Programmes for cultural understanding (schools, professional development, integration)
- Evaluation: integration success, service quality, economic benefit

## Frequently asked questions

**Should the national languages be replaced?**  
No. German, French, Italian and Romansh are part of Switzerland and will remain so. This is about an additional shared lingua franca for daily life, business and science — not about displacement.

**Why English?**  
Because it is today's most practical bridge language: in science and innovation, in international business, and in exchange across Europe and globally.

**Isn't this a culture-war topic?**  
No — language is infrastructure. It determines whether people feel welcome, whether work succeeds and whether institutions are comprehensible. We treat it as a project of understanding, not an identity fight.

**How will this be implemented?**  
Step by step and measurably: multilingual government information where it has impact, voluntary learning pathways, recognition of language competences — and evaluation of integration success, service quality and economic benefit.

# Not left. Not right. Future-ready.

> Why The Future doesn't fit the left-right spectrum — and how we make decisions instead.

Source: https://die-zukunft.ch/en/beyond-left-right/ · Publisher: The Future (Swiss political party, Basel)

## Not left. Not right. Future-ready.

Today's politics often operates on reflexes: left versus right, crisis versus crisis, camp versus camp. This produces noise — but too rarely solutions. **The Future** doesn't fit neatly into the left-right spectrum, because the major challenges of our time operate on different axes:

- **Sovereignty** vs. dependency
- **Functionality** vs. bureaucracy
- **Transparency** vs. black box
- **Abundance** vs. scarcity thinking
- **Courage to implement** vs. symbolic politics

## Our Anti-Ideology Promise

Ideology becomes an obstacle when it prevents things from working. Our benchmark is: **What makes life better — measurably, robustly, scalably?**

## How We Make Decisions

Our criteria:

- **Effectiveness**: Is there a real effect in everyday life?
- **Feasibility**: Is it implementable — legally, financially, operationally?
- **Sovereignty**: Does it make us more or less dependent in critical areas?
- **Freedom & Dignity**: Does it expand room to act and security?
- **Transparency**: Is it verifiable, auditable, correctable?

## The Typical Labels

Why they don't fit:

### "Tech-libertarian?"

No. We are not "state out, market in." We want a **capable state** that creates security, reduces dependencies and enforces transparency — especially for critical infrastructure. Freedom without sovereignty is an illusion.

### "Socialist?"

No. We are not for planned economies or ideology. Our focus is **abundance through productivity** — and a welfare state that empowers people, instead of trapping them in bureaucracy.

### "Neoliberal?"

No. We are not for deregulation at any cost. Where markets work: fine. Where lock-in, monopolies or dependencies emerge: **rules, standards, exit obligations, competition**.

## Examples Showing Why We Don't Fit the Spectrum

- **Digital Sovereignty**: not "statist" and not "market-fundamentalist" — but anti-lock-in, pro open standards, pro security.
- **Re-industrialisation via Robotics**: pro productivity and prosperity, but SME-friendly, socially secured, without fear of decline.
- **Basic Income (Pilot)**: a safety foundation that reduces bureaucracy and facilitates entrepreneurship — without moral debates, with measurement instead of dogma.
- **Cities & Housing**: pro densification at transit hubs (including height), so housing becomes more affordable and sprawl is reduced.
- **Life Science & Health**: pro progress, but with clear limits: no black-box state, opt-in default, transparency.

## What We Reject

- **Fear-based politics** as a permanent state
- **Symbolic politics** without impact
- **Black-box systems** in government and health
- **Culture wars** as a substitute for shaping the future

## What We Stand For

A state that makes change possible, rather than merely administering it. A Switzerland that remains sovereign and cooperates constructively with Europe. A society that translates abundance into prosperity, comfort and well-being. If you've had enough of tribal politics: welcome.

---

# Votes

> Swiss federal popular votes — overview of proposals, framed along The Future's twelve pillars. No voting recommendation, with a program perspective.

Source: https://die-zukunft.ch/en/abstimmungen/ · Publisher: The Future (Swiss political party, Basel)

Switzerland votes on federal proposals four times a year. This page is a permanent overview: for each voting Sunday, a short framing per proposal along the twelve pillars of our [program](@/programm.en.md). We deliberately don't issue voting recommendations yet: ballot positions belong to a democratic party process with members and assemblies — and as a young party, we are building exactly that. Until then, we describe where a proposal meets the program and what tension sits behind it.

---

## Next vote — 29 November 2026

Four proposals are on the ballot. The full framing is in the article [29 November 2026 vote: four proposals, five pillars](@/aktuelles/abstimmung-29-november-2026.en.md).

**Federal decree on additional financing of the AHV through a VAT increase.** Seeks to top up old-age pension funding through a higher VAT; as a constitutional amendment it goes to a mandatory popular vote. Consumption rather than wages as the financing base fits our logic — the tension is the partial funding: together with the federal contribution about half of the cost, the rest stays open. → Pillars [Basic income](@/grundeinkommen.en.md) and [Open government](@/offener-staat.en.md). Federal Council and Parliament: yes.

**Popular initiative "For a restriction of fireworks".** Seeks a nationwide ban on the sale and use of loud fireworks by private individuals. Names a real problem of densified cities — the tension is the level: a constitutional article for a rule municipalities can set themselves today. → Pillar [Cities & housing](@/stadte-wohnen.en.md). Federal Council and Parliament: no.

**Popular initiative "Yes to fair federal taxes for married couples too – end the discrimination of marriage!".** Seeks to abolish the marriage penalty in direct federal tax while keeping joint assessment of married couples — a different model from the individual taxation accepted in March. The goal is settled — the tension is the duplication: two systems for the same people, with losses of up to 3 billion. → Pillar [Open government](@/offener-staat.en.md). Federal Council and Parliament: no.

**Amendment to the Federal Act on War Material.** Seeks to relax war material export rules: deliveries to partner states even in a conflict, fewer non-re-export declarations, and a clause letting the Federal Council deviate from the licensing criteria in extraordinary circumstances; a referendum brings the proposal to the people. Protective capability needs an industrial base — the tension is control: executive discretion instead of clear rules in the law. → Pillars [Neutrality & peace](@/neutralitaet-frieden.en.md) and [Energy & resilience](@/energy-resilience.en.md). Federal Council and Parliament: yes.

---

## Last vote — 27 September 2026

Two popular initiatives, both rejected. The full framing is in the article [27 September 2026 vote: two initiatives, three pillars](@/aktuelles/abstimmung-27-september-2026.en.md).

**Popular initiative "Preserving Swiss neutrality (Neutrality Initiative)".** Sought to enshrine perpetual, armed neutrality in the constitution and to rule out military alliances and coercive measures not mandated by the UN. The goals largely overlap with our program — the tension lies in the sanctions clause and in the ban on cooperation, which could hamper defensive cooperation against hybrid threats. → Pillars [Neutrality & peace](@/neutralitaet-frieden.en.md) and [Energy & resilience](@/energy-resilience.en.md). People: no (70.2%), cantons: all no.

**Popular initiative "For secure nutrition (Nutrition Initiative)".** Sought a net self-sufficiency rate of at least 70 percent within ten years, more plant-based food and clean drinking water. Names a real dependence but sets a target without a plan: supply becomes more secure through technology and stockpiling, not through a number in the constitution. → Pillars [Energy & resilience](@/energy-resilience.en.md) and [Life science & health](@/life-science.en.md). People: no (72.5%), cantons: all no.

---

## Before that — 14 June 2026

Two proposals, two results. The full framing is in the article [14 June 2026 vote: two proposals, three pillars](@/aktuelles/abstimmung-14-juni-2026.en.md).

**Popular initiative "No to a Switzerland with 10 million!"** A rigid population cap pulls the wrong lever: the honest problem is infrastructure, not headcount. → Pillars [Talent & integration](@/talent-integration.en.md) and [Cities & housing](@/stadte-wohnen.en.md). People: no (54.8%).

**Amendment to the Civilian Service Act.** Higher admission hurdles to civilian service — real tension between army strength and civil resilience. → Pillar [Neutrality & peace](@/neutralitaet-frieden.en.md). People: yes (53.0%).

---

## Before that — 8 March 2026

Five proposals, three results that count long-term.

**Cash initiative.** Anchor cash in the constitution. → Pillar [Digital sovereignty](@/digitale-souveraenitaet.en.md). People: no.

**Cash counter-proposal.** Protect cash without a rigid quantity rule. → Pillar [Digital sovereignty](@/digitale-souveraenitaet.en.md). People: yes.

**SBC initiative.** Cap the radio and TV licence fee at 200 francs per year. → Pillar [Language & understanding](@/sprache-verstaendigung.en.md). People: no.

**Climate Fund initiative.** Federal fund for climate-protection investments. → Pillar [Energy & resilience](@/energy-resilience.en.md). People: no.

**Individual taxation.** Separate tax assessment for married couples. → Pillar [Open state](@/offener-staat.en.md). People: yes.

---

## Why this tracker exists

Federal popular votes are Switzerland's most important steering instrument. They come in dense succession — four dates a year, often two to five proposals per date. Anyone who does not follow politics full-time loses the overview fast.

This page is our contribution to civil attention: a compact framing per proposal, always along the same twelve pillars. No voting recommendation. For the full text and official arguments, see [admin.ch](https://www.admin.ch/) and [easyvote.ch](https://www.easyvote.ch/).
